cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I texted that I'd lost my job. You replied, 'What's for dinner?' Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Making your dinner? Can you see why I felt like the cook?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believe you. Before you book, can you see why I heard a chore? I needed you to ask how I was.

mechanism: A manages the dinner conversation but accepts B practical clarification while keeping attention on why the original text felt like another demand.
confusable: Unlike proving malicious intent, A asks for acknowledgment of the hurt despite corrected intent; borrowed authority concedes the meal plan to retain the emotional discussion.
comparison: Job-loss text and dinner misunderstanding differ from the irreplaceable concert guest.
seedUse: Use D99-b job loss/dinner/normality/restaurant and S02-b practical concession without surrendering the needed topic.
